short: He destroyed the Assassins and the Abbasid Caliphate, and founded Mongol rule in Persia.
full:
Möngke sent his brother west in 1253 with a fifth of the empire's fighting men and instructions to subdue everything as far as Egypt. Hulagu took the Ismaili fortresses of the Assassins one by one, Alamut surrendering in 1256, and burned their library. He then demanded submission from the Abbasid caliph al-Musta'sim, took Baghdad in February 1258, and had the caliph killed — by tradition rolled in a carpet and trampled, so that no royal blood touched the ground. Aleppo fell in 1260 and Damascus opened its gates.

News of Möngke's death took Hulagu and most of his army back east, and the detachment left behind under Kitbuqa was destroyed at Ain Jalut in September 1260. He never resumed the advance: his cousin Berke of the Golden Horde, a Muslim outraged by Baghdad, attacked him in the Caucasus instead. Hulagu ruled Persia, Iraq and much of Anatolia as ilkhan — subordinate khan — until his death on 8 February 1265, patronising astronomers at the new observatory at Maragheh.
